summary: We developed 'field-turn', which is a free-to-access web tool that uses NASA earth data to generate area-specific crop rotation advice for farmers around the globe. It deals with the challenge directly by providing an all-in-one tool for the farmers to navigate through changing temperatures, rainfall patterns and soil health etc while also providing practical rotation strategies that would be best suitable specifically for that field and that farmer, considering all the future challenges and farmer priorities(income, water conservation etc.). This is really important because it dumbs down all the available data into a form that the farmers can easily interpret and hence implement to adapt to changing environmental conditions and be prepared weeks in advance for any harsh climatic conditions.
details:
What it does:

FieldTurn helps farmers make informed crop rotation decisions using real NASA data. Farmers simply tap their field on the map or select their location to access climate and soil information specific to their area.

The platform combines historical data from NASA POWER, including temperature, rainfall, evapotranspiration and soil moisture, with recent weather conditions and satellite imagery from NASA GIBS. It transforms these complex datasets into simple visuals, including rainfall and temperature charts, colour-coded growing-season calendars, heat and frost risk indicators, and rainfall-versus-crop-water-requirement graphs.

Based on this information, FieldTurn generates three crop rotation plans: soil-building, water-saving and pest-break. Each recommendation is tailored to the field's climate and seasons, with an explanation of its benefits. An offline-capable assistant also guides farmers through their choices and answers questions in simple language.

Benefits/impact:

Crop rotation decisions often require agricultural expertise and access to data that many farmers lack. FieldTurn aims to make these resources accessible to everyone. It is free, requires no login, works on mobile devices and supports English, Urdu and Hindi, including right-to-left text. Its graphics-first approach also makes information easier to understand for users with different literacy levels.

Our goal is to help farmers improve soil health, reduce water consumption, minimise pest outbreaks and maintain more stable crop yields. With globally available NASA datasets, FieldTurn has the potential to support farming communities worldwide

Tools/tech:

FieldTurn is built using a single HTML, CSS and JavaScript page, with no backend or installation required. It uses Leaflet for interactive mapping, Esri/Maxar satellite imagery with an OpenStreetMap fallback, NASA POWER for climate data and NASA GIBS for satellite imagery.

All agricultural calculations run directly in the browser, including FAO-56 Hargreaves evapotranspiration, growing-season detection and crop rotation recommendations. This lightweight design makes the platform easy to host and usable even with unreliable internet connectivity.

Considerations:

We designed FieldTurn with an Apple-inspired liquid-glass interface, placing an interactive satellite map behind the controls to create a clean and intuitive experience.

Accessibility and scientific accuracy were equally important. We incorporated multilingual support, visual explanations and clear data labels while carefully distinguishing average and extreme climate values. Recommendations are also season-aware and account for rainfall and crop water requirements.

Our biggest challenge was simplifying complex scientific information without compromising its accuracy. That gap is bridged through field-turn by transforming NASA's environmental data into practical decisions that the farmers can actually implement.
